descriptions.shortDescription: Business process and workflow management for Nextcloud.
descriptions.longDescription: Dossiq is a business process and workflow management application for Nextcloud. It enables organisations to model, execute, and monitor business processes and workflows. Built on Open Register, it integrates with the Nextcloud ecosystem and supports process automation and standardisation for both government and commercial organisations.

Dossiq is een bedrijfsprocesbeheers- en workflowtoepassing voor Nextcloud. Het stelt organisaties in staat bedrijfsprocessen en workflows te modelleren, uit te voeren en te monitoren. Gebouwd op Open Register integreert het met het Nextcloud-ecosysteem en ondersteunt procesautomatisering en -standaardisatie voor zowel overheids- als commerciële organisaties.

sources.subject: ConductionNL/dossiq
sources.caveat: Authors of the latest 1000 commits of the last 12 months, told apart by address after the repository's .mailmap. Their organisation is the domain of their address, or for a personal, hidden or noreply address the company on their public profile. The owning organisation (conduction.nl) is the most common organisation domain, the domains and names in publiccode.yml and the owner account; one person with two addresses counts twice. Bots are left out.

results.title: Project health (CHAOSS)
results.description: How active and widely carried the project is: the bus factor, the spread over organisations, how change requests and issues are handled, and how often it releases. Informative: shown, not rated.
results.message: 6 of 6 CHAOSS metrics measured. They are shown for information and do not count in any rating.

metrics.name: Contributor Absence Factor
metrics.explanation: The fewest people who together made half of the commits on the default branch in the last 12 months, of the 100 contributors GitHub reports, among 7 human contributors. At 1 the project depends on a single person. Bots are left out; one person with several accounts or addresses counts more than once.

metrics.name: Organizational Diversity
metrics.explanation: Organisations are told apart by the email domain of the latest 300 commits of the last 12 months (258 commits by people, after the .mailmap) and, for a personal or hidden address, by the company on the author's public profile. The largest is conduction.nl (3 authors), with 100% of the 258 commits whose organisation is known; 0% of the commits come from 0 of 3 authors whose organisation stays unknown. Only these counts are kept, no names, addresses or companies; an organisation is named only when several authors share it.

metrics.name: Change Request Closure Ratio
metrics.explanation: 3,895 change requests were closed (merged or not) and 3,983 opened in the last 90 days, bots included. Below 1 the open backlog grows; above 1 it shrinks.

metrics.name: Time to First Response
metrics.explanation: None of the 15 latest change requests opened by people between 2026-08-21 and 2026-11-12 got a comment or review from anyone but its author.

metrics.name: Issue Response Time
metrics.explanation: None of the 15 latest issues opened by people between 2026-08-21 and 2026-11-12 got a comment from anyone but its author.

metrics.name: Release Frequency
metrics.explanation: 5 final releases were published in the last 12 months, about one every 73 days, counted from the GitHub releases. The latest final release is from 2026-09-06. Besides these, 1,055 pre-releases were published; they are not counted. Drafts and pre-releases are left out.

notes: Measured over the open issues and the issues closed in the last 90 days, in working days (Monday to Friday, Europe/Amsterdam, without Dutch public holidays).
Only the 200 most recently updated issues of each kind were read.

Vulnerabilities are read from the published GitHub security advisories, from draft to publication. Their response time, unpublished advisories and Dependabot alerts need admin rights and are not measured.
No issue carries a blocking label (such as blocker or critical), so every bug counts as an other bug.
